chunks: And from him, from Ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about breast-feeding, what is the least of it that prohibits [marriage]? He (peace be upon him) said: 'That which builds the flesh and the blood.' Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you consider one [session] to build it?' So I said, 'I ask you, may Allah improve you, what about two?' He said, 'No.' And I did not cease to count/reiterate to him until it reached ten breast-feedings.

key_terms.أَنْبَتَ اللَّحْمَ وَ الدَّمَ: Built the flesh and the blood

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum number of breast-feedings required to establish a mahram relationship in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the juristic criteria for establishing the mahram relationship through radāʿ, defining the threshold as the quantity sufficient to 'nourish flesh and blood.' The dialogue with Ubayd ibn Zurara demonstrates the scholarly method of refining legal definitions, moving from a qualitative measure to the widely accepted quantitative standard of ten feedings in Shia fiqh. This establishes the foundational principle that mere ingestion is insufficient; the nutritional impact must be significant enough to contribute to physical development.
